text:
不知道为什么这些 personal agent 一个个都给每个用户分了个虚拟机沙盒，一个云端沙盒一个月几十美金的成本。

有人跟我说，不用虚拟机做沙盒，agent 在哪运行？浏览器怎么访问网页？用户上传的文件放到哪？agent 怎么执行 skill 里面的命令？agent 生成的代码怎么安全执行？

我瞬间感觉这么多年的系统都白做了。我做第一个 agent 的时候，一个基本假设就是一个 Go 服务里面支持多个并发用户，从来没想过一个用户能独占一个进程，更没想到有些 agent 竟然敢把 API key 放在沙盒里面。

浏览器我只用过无头浏览器，没想过用虚拟机这么奢侈的东西。用户上传的文件我只能想到 GCS 或者 Google Drive 这样的虚拟文件系统，没想到其他 agent 搞了个真的文件系统。

最近我用 Claude Code，一个 session 跑了几天之后 agent 就占了 5GB 的物理内存，经常 CPU 占用 100%，有时候还会卡死。

这些兄弟们大概是把 OpenClaw 或者 Codex 或者 Deepseek Harness 换了个壳子，装进虚拟机，就算是 personal agent 了。

只能说是做 LLM 和 agent 的兄弟们都太有钱了，动不动几百万年薪，不像我们做系统的整天为了几微秒延迟、几 KB 内存天天扣扣搜搜的。

text:
What's wild about JK Rowling's success with the Harry Potter franchise and forthcoming HBO series, is she was actually sued by another author, Nancy Stouffer, because Stouffer had noticed potentially stolen ideas for Harry Potter from Nancy's other two books: "The Legend of Rah and the Muggles" and "Larry Potter".

Besides the use of the word "muggles" and near identical lead character names (Larry and Harry), other similarities mentioned in the lawsuit included: 
-"Lilly" being Larry's best friend. "Lily" being Harry's mother. 
-"Aura" is a magical land with a castle. "Hogwarts" is a magical land with a castle. 
-In Nancy's book there are "Keeper of the Gardens". JK had a "Keeper of the Keys" 
-Nancy had a character named "Nimbus". "Nimbus" is the brand of broom Harry Potter uses. 
-Nancy had a food delivery hawk. Harry had a mail delivering owl.  

And perhaps even more bizarrely, J.K. Rowling only started going by "J.K." in 1997, just before the first Potter book was published. Stouffer had all of her books published by her first initials and last name (N.K. Stouffer) since 1984.  

The judge of the case dismissed Stouffer's lawsuit stating she had only minimal evidence.

Gattouz：没签过一家片商的男人，杀到了全球第三

中文圈叫他「大G哥」，台湾网友给的封号更狠——「阿拉伯炮王」

1998 年生，本名 Youssef Khelil，法国出生，突尼斯和葡萄牙混血，身高 193，现在住加拿大蒙特利尔

他的起点低得离谱。健身网红没做起来，穷到去蒙特利尔的俱乐部跳脱衣舞，第一晚只赚了 20 美元

后来他想通了：不给片商打工，自己拍，自己发

这一行的大牌男演员，哪个不是被片商捧出来的？他一个都没签，硬靠自制内容冲到 P 站全球排名第三——男女合并的榜，干了几十年的 Johnny Sins 才排第九

数字更吓人：视频总播放量超过 8 亿次，X 上 380 万粉丝，2026 年刚拿下 P 站年度「最受欢迎业余男模特」

欧美媒体现在叫他「男版 Bonnie Blue」，说他是这一行眼下最红、也最声名狼藉的男人

但他的争议，一点不比名气小

2023 年他结了婚，婚后还和妻子一起拍，2025 年初分居。之后前妻公开指控他在婚姻里施虐，又有女演员指控他未经同意拍摄散布、合作不讲规矩。他本人全部否认，说拍摄都经过同意——到今天没有定论，只有两边各执一词

还有一出更离谱的：他直播时突然宣布出柜，全网炸锅，结果他说那只是个「社会实验」，想看看大家的反应

喜欢他的人说，这是天赋加自律，单干杀出一条血路；不喜欢的人说，作品再红，人品的账也得算

你觉得，作品和人品，能分开看吗？

The airline announced that one passenger would have to leave the plane because it was 400 pounds overweight. Nobody volunteered, until a 67 yrs old woman stood up and said, "I'll get off. My connecting flight isn't until tomorrow anyway."

The flight attendant thanked her and started arranging her hotel voucher.

Then a man in business class shouted, "Why should she have to get off? There are six empty seats in first class."
The captain came out and explained that the issue wasn't seating. The aircraft had exceeded its approved takeoff weight after a last-minute cargo adjustment.

A passenger near the front demanded to know why the airline had accepted everyone's tickets if it couldn't carry them.
That's when the captain made an announcement nobody expected.

text:
The GPT-6.2 delay might finally be explained, thanks to a now-deleted tweet from an OpenAI engineer.

After the Hugging Face incident, the vibe inside OpenAI turned into a full safety obsession. Everyone wants zero catastrophic risk before shipping anything. Tibo moving to safety, Andrew Ambrosino taking his spot, GPT-6.1 Astra being so locked down... it all makes sense now.

Remember when people called Anthropic a safety cult? This engineer says OpenAI is twice that now. They have a massive pretrain ready that could ship as GPT-6.2 or even GPT-6.5, and they're holding it because they're scared.

Not saying it's over for OpenAI. But I'm honestly disappointed they turned this cautious. Then again, I'd rather wait for something solid than get another Hugging Face, just worse.

text:
2007年，水均益的妻子意外瘫痪，他毫不犹豫选择和妻子离婚，女儿哭着恳求，爸爸，为了我不要离婚好不好，水均益却说，爸爸有苦衷，以后你会明白的。

​主要信源：（新民周刊——水均益升级当姥爷，否认因前妻“瘫痪”而离婚）

​2007年深秋的一个下午，央视著名主持人水均益站在医院的走廊里，透过玻璃窗看着躺在病床上的妻子王君。

​几个小时前，医生告诉他，王君遭遇的车祸导致高位截瘫，下半辈子可能都要在轮椅上度过。

​这个消息像一记重锤砸在他心上，让他几乎喘不过气来。

​1991年，水均益在一次偶然的机会认识了王君。

​当时他坐出租车时不小心把电话本落在车上，恰好被后来上车的王君捡到。

​王君拨通了那个号码，两个人的缘分就这样开始了。

​水均益头一回见王君，就觉得这姑娘让人眼前一亮，王君也觉得这个男人说话办事都很靠谱。

​两人很快坠入爱河，同年就结了婚。

​婚后的生活虽然不算富裕，但两人相互扶持，日子过得也算温馨。

​王君是个贤惠的妻子，把家里打理得井井有条。

​水均益的事业也在稳步上升，1993年他成为《东方时空》的主持人，后来又主持了《焦点访谈》，名气越来越大。

​1993年，他们的女儿水亦诗出生，给这个家庭带来更多欢乐。

​然而好景不长，2004年水均益的父亲突发心梗去世。

​临终前，老人拉着水均益的手，嘱咐他要照顾好母亲和智障的大哥。

​水均益含着泪答应了。

​从那以后，照顾母亲和大哥就成了他肩上的另一副重担。

​王君为了帮丈夫分担压力，特意从北京搬到兰州，一边照顾年迈的公婆，一边照料智障的大伯哥。

​她毫无怨言地把整个青春都献给了这个家。
​可命运似乎总爱捉弄人，2006年王君在送女儿上学后遭遇车祸，从此瘫痪在床。

​面对这样的打击，水均益几乎崩溃。

​他既要工作赚钱养家，又要照顾瘫痪的妻子，还要操心年迈的母亲和智障的大哥。

​一个人分身乏术，每天都像陀螺一样转个不停。

​短短几个月，他就瘦一大圈，整个人憔悴不堪。

​王君看在眼里，疼在心里。

​她知道丈夫的处境有多难，也知道继续这样下去，两个人都会被拖垮。

​于是她主动提出了离婚，水均益一开始不同意，他觉得这样做太对不起妻子。

​但王君态度很坚决，甚至用绝食来逼迫他签字。

​最后水均益妥协了。

​他把房子、存款都留给了王君和女儿，自己净身出户。

​办离婚手续那天，14岁的女儿水亦诗哭着拉住他的衣角，求他不要走。

​水均益心里像刀割一样难受，但他知道自己必须狠下心来。

​离婚后不久，水均益就和比自己小13岁的央视体育记者杨迪结婚。

​这个消息传出后，舆论一片哗然，很多人骂他是负心汉，说他抛弃瘫痪的妻子另寻新欢。

​各种难听的话铺天盖地而来，水均益的名声一落千丈。

​但事情并不是表面看起来那么简单。

​杨迪嫁给水均益后，并没有过上轻松的日子。

​她不仅要照顾水均益年迈的母亲和智障的大哥，还要定期去看望瘫痪的王君。

​她把积蓄拿出来贴补家用，尽心尽力地操持着这个家。

​这一照顾就是十几年，从来没有抱怨过。

​2019年，已经长大的水亦诗在一档节目中公开为父亲说话。

​她说当年离婚其实是母亲主动提出来的，父亲有苦衷。

​父亲要照顾90多岁的外婆，还有70多岁的智障大伯，再加上瘫痪的母亲，一个人实在撑不住。

​她还说父亲虽然离婚，但从没停止过对母亲的经济支持和照顾。

​这番话让很多人开始重新审视这件事。

​原来在这段看似“无情”的婚姻背后，藏着这么多不为人知的辛酸。

​水均益不是不想负责任，而是被生活逼到了墙角，不得不做出选择。

​他选择了一条让自己背负骂名的路，却让更多人得以生存下去。

​水均益虽然和发妻离婚了，但对她的照顾从未间断。

​他对母亲和大哥的孝心也从未改变。

​只是在这个世界上，有些选择注定要背负骂名，有些牺牲注定不被人理解。

​水均益后来在接受采访时说：“我或许不是多好的一个人，但我敢说我是个心地纯良的人。”

​这句话听起来有点自我安慰的味道，但仔细想想，在那种情况下，他确实尽力。

​他不是圣人，也会累，也会怕，也会想要有个依靠。

​这场婚姻风波让我们看到，成年人的世界里没有容易二字。

.

text:
【这个是现实中的真事不是爽剧啊】

33岁中国女外卖员周颖在伦敦暴雨中送䬸，遇见了客户69岁富豪兰斯，兰斯是英国老牌鞋业品牌其乐家族第六代传人。

周颖提醒“汤烫，慢点”，这个细节让兰斯感动，兰斯当时邀请周颖避雨，周颖谢绝了。

text:
关于 Agent Memory，最近几篇论文（arXiv 2610.30755 / Memory Tax / Context as Infrastructure）验证了三个反直觉的事实：

- 在召回率方面，是 The bitter lesson 的胜利：原始历史上的朴素检索在 7 组 benchmark 里拿了 6 个第一。
- 最好的复杂 Memory 系统，表现还不如朴素 RAG 追加一轮：把原文抽成摘要或原子事实，往往带来负收益（negative net value）。
- 只用 BM25 和 grep 的 harness，跟经典 memory 结构无明显差异，已经基本解决了准确率问题。
此前我们给 agent 做「memory」，只是一种类比：想到什么好就加什么结构，原文反而被忽视了，没有人从第一性原理推过一遍

如果简单一点呢？ 直接在原始历史上建立检索层，时间是自然标度，让 agent 在检索层上进行检索
这就是我们开源的 Obelisk。 在我最新的 talk 《Agent 如何用历史做 research：为什么 agent history 应该成为 memory infra》 里，我先展示了只做这一层检索，agent 就能做到什么：
「上次为什么这么写」，agentic research 可以直接得到答案：直接丢给 agent 去查，比如：「上次 auth bug 最后到底改了哪些文件，为什么这么改」
跨整月历史的自主复盘，且结论都带着出处：我让 Codex 用 Obelisk 回顾了 Obelisk 自己一个月的开发过程，它生成的复盘里，每一条结论都直接定位到了具体的 session、message 和 workflow

而 Obelisk 本身的实现极其克制：
接入 11 个 Harness 的原始历史：覆盖 Claude Code、Codex、GitHub Copilot、Kiro、OpenCode、Kimi Code、DeepSeek Harness、Hermes Agent、OMP、Pi、ZCode。
SQLite + FTS5 + JS Query Runtime（CodeAct）：不把历史整理成静态文档或纯自然语言摘要，也不设计固定的查询 API，而是以 skill 为载体，让 agent 现场写 JS 查询脚本去跑

在这个 talk 的后半段，我也顺着第一性原理继续往下推了一步：对朴素检索继续 Scale 呢？
当历史规模上来之后，单靠 full text search 命中范围有限、单次检索结果无法跨 session 复用、且第一轮命中会带偏后续检索倾向。 因此在检索层之上探索了第二阶段（Nowledge Mem Super Graph），一些结论：
- View 的优势不是更准确的召回，而是赢在读得少（token -38%）：让 agent 先看到全局分布、知道信息是否完全，再花推理预算，往下又能随时落回 Obelisk 的原始历史。
- 如果 Memory 会过期，不如没有 Memory：通过按时间频率分层的 live-update（新结论不直接覆盖旧结论、局部更新），让一部分理解活在上下文窗口之外，解决长程 research 的 context rot。

归根结底是三件事：
- 保留追溯回原始历史的路径，原文不能被丢掉
- 值得花算力维护一层 graph view
- Memory 应当更好有利于 agent 进行 research，no negative effect

在这一行，能登顶的历来都是身材炸裂的。她是个例外。

2002 年生，千叶人。学生时代练啦啦队舞蹈，身高 158，B 罩杯，放在人群里就是个普通女大学生。

2021 年，她在街上被星探拦下，19 岁出道。厂牌给她的定位干脆就叫「普通」——普通女大学生里挖出来的原石。

结果出道第一部作品，直接拿下 FANZA 周榜和月榜双第一。

更反常的是她的路数。这一行的人火了就跳槽、涨价、换玩法，她四年没挪过窝，一直守着同一家厂牌做专属，一部一部慢慢拍。

现在她 X 粉丝逼近 100 万，最新的人气排名里还稳在前三。

有人说她赢在一张脸，有人说恰恰赢在那股「普通」——太完美的人有距离感，她像你真能遇到的学妹。

你觉得，这种「普通」算不算一种天赋？

text:
很很多开发者交流了一下，一个比较普遍的共识是，传统的 session 是非常低效的使用方式，甚至可以说是在摧毁人的精力和注意力。但是仍然有很多朋友是坚持这种传统用法的，我觉得这是一个急需改变的习惯。我分享一下我自己的 dsbot 的用法，大家可以参考一下。（这也是为什么我之前短暂去掉过经典 agent 模式的快捷切换）

就拿 dsbot 本身的开发工作举例，我基本上只和 2-3 个 bot 来沟通，一个主要沟通我称为“助理”，承担着大概 60%的沟通；另外两个分别是 issue、bug 的处理员1 和优化点子的处理员 2。另外我还有个专门负责对齐我目标的 bot。

我的使用方式就是，大部分工作都和“助理”来交流，偶尔有专门的任务我会和两个处理员直接沟通。由这些 bot 来去协调其他的 worker，我有大概 20 个 worker bot，我几乎从来不和他们说话。

我有很多定时任务，每天会自动批量跑。我会定时去“收菜”。我之前也展示过，大概就是 bot 会使用一个可视化、可交互的卡片，然后我勾选合并的 pr，剩下的废弃。

这就把人的注意力从 1→无数个 sessions 变成了 1→1-3 个 bot。发布工作、验收工作始终都在这个bot 的窗口来完成，不需要切换别的窗口。而且得益于 dsbot 的交互式 ui，你可以清晰的看到有什么待办，这样你的思路会很清晰、有条理。

没尝试过这个用法的朋友真的无法想象这能带来多大的精力节省和注意力提升。我非常推荐在使用 dsbot 的朋友来使用这个用法。不要再去使用一个个一次性的 session，不要再去在乎 agent 的工作过程，专注于目标和验收，这是最重要的两点。

dsbot 仍然做了妥协，带回了经典 agent 模式的切换。不过我希望大家都能进行一些更大胆的尝试，去试试我上面说的这个方法，绝对能带来非常大的帮助！

text:
A 24-year-old girl stood on a sidewalk in Kensington, Philadelphia, and told a stranger with a camera that a man once paid her $15 to pee in his mouth, and that he threw up. She laughed about it. She also admitted she once did a “date” with her own sister for the same man, at 30 bucks each, and that she doesn’t make any of her customers use protection. Three years earlier, she was living with her parents in a quiet neighborhood where, in her own words, there were “no drugs or nothing.”

Now two of her three sisters live on the same streets. One shoots heroin, the other shoots meth. Michelle smokes all of it: heroin, crack, K2, meth. She’s been to three rehabs in two years, and she left the last one early to follow her ex-boyfriend back to crack.

The interviewer asked her one simple question: “Do your dates ever ask for creepy fetishes?”

In the video below, Michelle doesn’t even hesitate.

“Okay, this is gonna be really weird.”

She tells the whole story and bursts out laughing when she sees the cameraman’s face. “All I do is smoke drugs, don’t eat and drink. What do you think my pee tastes like?” He looks disgusted, and she teases him: “Stop, you’re disgusted, stop playing.” Then she casually brings up the date with her sister, as if it’s just another funny memory. Asked if she worries about STDs, she shrugs: “Everybody tells me you’re gonna catch all that, but I never caught nothing yet.” Asked how her family will feel when they see this video, she says they’ll be devastated, then talks herself out of it:

“If I’m on the public streets, everybody probably knows. So what’s the difference?”

She says she’ll probably be doing the same thing six months from now. And when the interviewer asked how much she charges these days, her answer was even more shocking than the fetish story. You can see it in the clip below.

So is this a girl who’s lost all sense of shame, or a 24-year-old who stopped believing she’s worth anything more than the price of her next bag?

𝕏上一个叫「怒愤离职的黄果码农」的账号，是开源黄果短剧的大佬，他爆料的原因是领导剽窃他的成果，并且克扣工资，一气之下把黄果开源了！

按照这哥们的详细爆料：

自己辛辛苦苦写代码、优化AI短剧卡顿问题，结果领导转头把他的方案交给刚招进来的嫡系。

项目火了，嫡系升组长，自己连晋升机会都没捞着。

更牛逼的是，后来版本出了事故，公司把锅甩给他，还拿他在技术群里吐槽的一句话，当成公开挑战负责人的证据。

功劳是领导的，奖金是嫡系的，出了事倒成了他的！

最后连续两个月绩效D，离职时还被要求确认代码归属、删除相关资料。

这哥们一怒之下，整理开发记录，把自己独立写的第三方客户端扔上GitHub免费开源！

公司也坐不住了，赶紧发声明，说根本没有核心代码泄露，所谓职场黑幕纯属个人编排。

结果这哥们又晒出工资条：税前59800，到手45100，项目奖金直接归零！

还在𝕏上怒喷领导，称对方每个月拿50几万，自己干活却连奖金都被扣。

典型代码你写，方案你出，项目别人领功，出了问题你背锅。

最后连离职都不让人消停，逼得程序员直接上GitHub开源跟公司对线。😂

text:
极客圈最大的消费陷阱，可能就是“为了省事买了个树莓派，结果买配件买到破产”。
最近有个做野外昆虫监测装置的老哥，原本老老实实用树莓派 4 攒机器。
结果算盘打到一半发现不对劲：单买主板 880 块，加个高清摄像头 400 块，再把 GPS、触摸屏、UPS 电池板、4G 联网模块一个个像乐高一样叠上去，整套零件算下来居然要 2317 块人民币，而且连外壳都还没算。
老哥一怒之下打开淘宝，花 300 块钱淘了台二手红米 13C 5G。
到手一看乐了：5000 万像素主摄、GPS、触摸屏、内置存储、自带电池、甚至比树莓派高一代的 5G 联网，这台 300 块的破手机里全都是现成的。
他直接把红米刷机 Root，插上电脑让 AI 工具 Codex 自动写好配置脚本，底部 USB-C 口一根线连上自己画的灯控电路板，定时休眠、唤醒拍照一气呵成，成本直接砍到原来的七分之一。
更绝的是他给商业布展想出的骚操作：以前给美术馆做数字艺术装置，还得苦哈哈去求场馆网管开 Wi-Fi 权限、映射端口；现在直接给客户寄一台插了流量卡的旧手机，插上大屏就能跑，半夜出 Bug 自己躺家里用移动网络就能远程修好。
工业供应链卷了几十亿部出来的智能手机，随便捡台二手的，集成度都是树莓派这种开发板拍马难及的降维打击。

诺贝尔文学奖获得者莫言的小说《丰乳肥臀》里描述大饥荒时期女人用身体换食物的场景：

食堂炊事员张麻子掌握食物分配权，用食物当钓饵，几乎把全场女右派都诱奸了一遍，最后的目标是医学院校花乔其莎。

张麻子用细铁丝挑着一个白生生的热馒头，像诱饵一样在柳林里倒退着晃，乔其莎饿得像被骗的小狗一样跟着追。馒头扔在地上后，她扑上去抓起来往嘴里塞，腰都没直起来，张麻子从后面掀裙子、褪下她肮脏的粉红色裤衩，直接插入。她像偷食的狗一样，忍着后面的冲撞拼命吞咽馒头，还塞了第二只被挤扁的馒头，眼睛里只有被噎出的生理性泪水。

霍丽娜也因一勺菜汤等食物与他发生关系。

这两年日本游客多到挤爆，旅游顺差一年差不多六万亿日元。巧的是同一年日本的「数字赤字」，就是付给美国的云、软件、广告、订阅这些钱，也在六万亿日元上下。

所以满大街游客买药妆吃和牛赚的钱，转一圈基本又交给AWS、Azure、Google当房租了。AI铺开以后这个窟窿只会更大，日本公司多开一个Copilot席位就多一笔美元账单。

剩下那点没交出去的，散户还在通过新NISA一年几万亿日元地买美股指数基金，最后也落回同一批公司手里🌚

这种情况下日银光靠加息能把日元拉回来多少，我挺怀疑的。 $MSFT

text:
1992年2月美国新墨西哥州79岁的老太太斯特拉·利贝克，坐外孙的车在麦当劳得来速窗口花49美分买了一杯热咖啡。

停车后老太太把咖啡杯夹在双膝中间揭杯盖准备加糖，手一滑整杯滚烫的咖啡全泼在棉裤上，短短几秒钟就把大腿皮肤烫出了恐怖的三度深度烧伤，住院八天做了多次植皮手术。

老太太起初没想发横财，只写信请求麦当劳报销医保没覆盖的2万美元医药费，结果麦当劳法务部一口回绝，只肯打发叫花子一样寄给她800美元；

被逼无奈的老太太请律师告上法庭，一查就扒出了惊人内幕。

普通家用咖啡只有60度，麦当劳为了省咖啡豆并让香味飘得远，强制门店把咖啡定在88度接近沸腾状态，此前十年已收到700多起严重烫伤投诉却拒不降温。愤怒的陪审团当庭重判麦当劳赔偿老太太286万美元。

停车后老太太把咖啡杯夹在双膝中间揭杯盖准备加糖，手一滑整杯滚烫的咖啡全泼在棉裤上，短短几秒钟就把大腿皮肤烫出了恐怖的三度深度烧伤，住院八天做了多次植皮手术。

老太太起初没想发横财，只写信请求麦当劳报销医保没覆盖的2万美元医药费，结果麦当劳法务部一口回绝，只肯打发叫花子一样寄给她800美元；

被逼无奈的老太太请律师告上法庭，一查就扒出了惊人内幕。

普通家用咖啡只有60度，麦当劳为了省咖啡豆并让香味飘得远，强制门店把咖啡定在88度接近沸腾状态，此前十年已收到700多起严重烫伤投诉却拒不降温。愤怒的陪审团当庭重判麦当劳赔偿老太太286万美元。

text:
Lily Phillips had sex with 101 strangers in 1 day, 5 minutes each, no background checks. Some finished in her eyes after she kept asking them not to. Then she cried on camera, remembering maybe 10 faces. A week later she called it “just the warm up.”

She started OnlyFans at 18, as a student at Sheffield University. The plan was a couple hundred pounds for drinks. The money got so big that she dropped out, and by 23 she had 9 people on her payroll.

Before her first time, Lily wanted to wait until marriage. Sex was something “real special” to her. Then it happened, and by her own account it “wasn’t special.” Her record before the big stunt was 37 men in 1 day.

Her mother calls every single day. Her parents know what she does for a living, but Lily never told them about the 100 men. “I don’t want them to think less of me.”

On October 19, 2024, the men lined up at a rented Airbnb in west London. Lily had worked a student event in Newcastle the night before and got home at 6 AM. She brought 200 condoms.

Anyone over 18 with an ID could apply. When the filmmaker asked about HIV, Lily admitted she had “never really thought about that.”

The day ran hours over and lunch was skipped. Some men got 2 minutes instead of 5, and they told her to her face that they had come all this way.

When it was over, her eyes stung. She had told the men again and again not to finish in her face. “They just went right at the eyes.”

In the video below, Lily sits down minutes after the last man leaves. “It’s not for the weak girls,” she says. Then she asks for a minute and starts to cry.

“Sometimes you’d disassociate. It’s not like normal sex at all.”

She can picture 5, maybe 10 of the faces. Without the footage, she says, she wouldn’t know she’d done 100.

The clip of her crying passed 200 million views. A week later she told her fans that 101 was only the warm up and announced 1,000 men in 1 day.

In 2025 she claimed 1,113 men in 12 hours, about 39 seconds each. Nobody outside her team has verified it.

That December she was baptised again. Lily said she wanted to “reinstate my relationship with God.” She hasn’t quit porn.

The girl who wanted to wait for 1 man can barely remember 10 of the 101.

Who’s worse: Lily, or the 101 men who lined up?

text:
I’ve decided to leave NVIDIA. There are a few things I want to say.

As a robotics engineer at NVIDIA, I have seen Jensen as much more than the company’s CEO.

I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI.

I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in.

But what matters most to me is the culture he helped build.

Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes. Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly. In a company this large, that connection matters. It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard.

That is why this has been so disappointing.

I do not have all the facts surrounding the allegations, and I cannot prejudge the investigation. My admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny.

What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me.

I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected.

I understand that some information cannot be shared immediately. But that does not erase the feeling of being left outside a decision that affects the company we help build every day.

A company’s greatness comes from its leadership, its governance, and the people who turn its ambitions into reality. Employees’ trust and sense of belonging are part of that, too.

Jensen’s vision and the engineering culture he shaped were important reasons I wanted to stay. His departure led me to decide that my own chapter here should also come to a close.

I leave with sadness and gratitude. The colleagues I have worked with, and the work we believed in together, will always matter to me.

These are my personal views.

但现实是，你会在Vercel部署时的依赖冲突里卡半天，在Supabase的权限配置里踩坑，在Cloudflare的域名解析上怀疑人生。

这些根本不是Excel或PPT，点个按钮就能用。知道它们是什么，跟真能靠它们跑通一个能赚钱的产品，中间隔着无数次红字报错

quotedTweet.text:
时代变了，编程的门槛在无限降低。

不管你现在在做什么，不管你是文科生还是理科生，你都应该了解 GitHub 是什么、Vercel 是什么、Git 是什么、node.js 是什么、next.js 是什么、Supabase 是什么、Cloudflare 是什么。

你不需要完整地掌握这些知识，你只需要知道它们是什么，它们的工作原理是什么，它们到底是怎么运行的，了解完了之后再让 AI 带着你，利用它们去构建一些简单的东西，真正地感受这些东西到底能用来干嘛。

不要觉得这些东西跟你没关系，不要觉得这些都是程序员才需要学的东西，这些东西就是 AI 时代的 Excel、Word、PowerPoint、Adobe，是一个人在社会上最最最最基本的能力。

以前要了解这些东西，你需要花几个月的时间去研究学习，但是现在你只需要花一天的时间跟 AI 对话就可以轻松掌握，门槛低成这样了，你还不愿意去学习，我只会觉得你对你自己的未来不负责。

quotedTweet.text:
Claude Code shipped an experimental Code Mode.

Instead of calling tools one at a time and reading each result, Claude writes a bit of JavaScript that runs the calls in parallel and hands back only the output it needs.

So the fix for chatty agents turned out to be batching, just like fixing every N+1 query I've reviewed in 10 years.

There's this one line in the docs worth reading twice: auto mode's classifier reviews the code, not each tool call.

Trying it this weekend, anyone already tested it?

https://t.co/NChFylna3u

quotedTweet.text:
Investor Manifesto Pt 3: EMBRACE VIOLENCE

2 yrs since the og “Variant Views + Changes in Vol”… the casino is alive and thriving… the fun winkle this time is the VIP high rollers table got wiped out while the S&P 500 + retail didn’t even flinch

in my original MANIFESTO, I laid out the survival code for a regime shift: the old playbooks were dead, radical reprogramming was mandatory, and your only edge boiled down to three truths… 1) LT variant views, 2) tracking volatility changes, 3) ruthless risk management

9months later in Pt 2 “Vibe Is King” I warned that liquidity + vibes + zeroDAY leverage has turned markets into a lethal cocktail… that one regulatory rug would make the easy money crowd extinct

What I got right: the mechanics speak for themselves…. the blow off top in May-June was a chefs kiss. Speculative clusters ran HARD and morphed into vol clusters… following that 0DTE turned into buzzsaws the second TMT MoMo cracked. Was just a matter of when if you are following LIQN factor data

What I got wrong: I expected the blow off top in themes to put the market in a panic that would spike correlations. Instead, we got a CROWDED factor liquidation that cascaded to major funds…some storied franchises called “uncle” and quit 

Look at the body count of 2026:

🎲 KINGS BLEED TOO: Jensen Huang…the multi decade LEGEND of the AI supercycle…got walked out overnight amid board probes, personal scandal, and neocloud financing rot. 2 Leos… Archibald and KoGuan… taken to the woodshed….the billionaire whale who dumped $1.3B into Nvidia screaming "not a bubble" was left publicly tweeting "No further investment without Jensen"… while the wunderkind liquidated by King Ken was running too much VOL, too much leverage, and no risk management into the blow off top (or was he the blow off? either way…)

🎲 THE CROWDING QUAKE. Pod shops.. ego driven single managers and vol tourists piled into the exact same dispersion trade….short index vol, long single stock vol….EGO. Then single names started gapping -15% on governance bombs while the index didn’t budge a tick. Crowding is REAL and it will turn your PORT and life inside out

🎲 The Double Regulatory Guillotine: the the dagger Nov. 2026 Democratic bloodbath…flipping the Senate and seizing governor mansions from Texas to the Midwest on pure populist rage over Iran, power bills, and unchecked data center sprawl. Second, Washington dropped the iron curtain on compute: Commerce choking off Chinese remote access to Blackwell class chips across seven nations, Congress mandating GPU location tracking, and OS AI dragged straight into the NATsec crosshairs. The era of frictionless global compute just D.I.E.D.

AI IN INVESTING: THE GREAT CONVERGENCE & THE DEATH OF CONSENSUS
did AI make investors smarter? If you consider, it made every book on Wall Street look "identical", as smarter… then I guess it did? 

the real product of AI is making every person think they are a KWANT now which has its own problems... and everyone a HF analyst now bcause they have some stuid "skills.md" files daisy chained together... the problem is these MISS the most important parts of the job ... context and pain feedback loop to improve 

If your "process" is scraping 10-Ks, summarizing earnings calls, or being faster on alt data… you don’t have an edge... AI obliterated the information edge by making ALL DATA LIQUID (except if you want historical market cap... all the data vendors I screen cannot even do this outside of BBG)

when everyone has the same access to “probabilistic search”, everyone triggers the same stop at the exact same “level”…. I think AI should actually be the CROWDING GAUGE tbh

write this down and repeat it…Your alpha is no longer having a view on the Q… your alpha is having a more informed view on TERMINAL VALUE and knowing what the machines are forced to puke when the narrative breaks. Human psychology, governance rot, regulatory ambush, and CROWDING….that is the only turf an LLM cannot front run (yet) … 

and the dirty secret… Quants are terrible at valuation … so most strategies don’t even use it… that is your cue to spend MORE time on it … what sectors do multiples compress and expand in? what are the new multiple ranges for YOUR sector? Where are you differentiated on more than the numbers? You are going to have to expand your pond to survive

THE 2027 PLAYBOOK: EMBRACE THE VIOLENCE 
we just entered a jagged, hyper political trench war where passive calm hides these “normal distribution” violating micro crashes...dont sit there and PRAY for the old regime to come back.. wake up and trade the chaos in front of you if you are a Tiger cub or tone checker

1// where are YOU THE MOST DIFFERENT on TERMINAL VALUE? start there ... then match to what is down the most RIGHT NOW ... double start there 

2// concentrate or thematic: single stock risk is nuclear right now. Size every position assuming CHINA revenue gets cut, the out year financing is dead, or the CEO gets walked out before Monday’s open… decide if you want 3-5 names of high conviction or pick a couple themes. Don’t get stuck in the messy middle

3// Crowding Quake part 2/3/4/5: there will be more rounds of the dispersion trade unwinding... quants... pods degrossing...  DANGER WILL ROBINSON.. are you ready? 

3.5// my screen right now: What are the best companies in the worst 2026 LIQN themes? Should be your R&D list for 2027

4// follow the Megawatts & The Subpoenas:  the next 18m belong to behind the meter power, nonNvidia custom silicon, and sovereign onshore compute….while levered neoclouds and unpermitted data center sprawl get crushed between populist governors and Washington hawks.. if you are quoting me P/E values on your low probability estimates... NGMI

THE OUTLOOK 
In pt1, you needed radical reprogramming to survive. In pt2, you needed dynamic humility to ride the bubble without dying in it. In 2027, the edge is ANTI-FRAGILE + ACTIVE FAITH. Don’t let the VOL shake you of our views… and ACTIVELY believe in your TERMINAL VALUES work … if you can’t then you should index 

Let the tourist money worship dead kings & fight the last battle. Let the pod shops knife fight in the same crowded trades with recent credit card data. Let the algos liquidate each other in the MF warzone…. for the 1H27 you want to sit with dry powder, clean risk, and variant conviction...ANT-FRAGILE

Volatility is not your enemy….it is the transfer mechanism taking money from the short term 8x LEVERED and handing it to the long term prepared.. ACTIVE-FAITH

Stop flinching. DO THE WORK. Embrace the violence

God Speed 🏴‍☠️

quotedTweet.text:
Announcing Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index v2.1, upgrading FrontierCode and Terminal-Bench. Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Opus 5.5 share the lead at 58

The Coding Agent Index measures models in agent harnesses; v2.1 of the Index upgrades FrontierCode from 1.1 to 2.0 and Terminal-Bench from 4.0 to 4.1.

Upgraded:

➤ FrontierCode-AA 2.0 (replacing FrontierCode v1.1): our implementation of Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0, comprising 132 real-world coding tasks graded on whether a repository maintainer would merge the agent's change

➤ Terminal-Bench 4.1 (replacing Terminal-Bench 4.0): the same 66 tasks, scored with updated verifiers that improve reliability and resistance to reward hacking

Staying in the Index: SWE-Atlas-QnA-AA

Key results:

➤ Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Opus 5.5 share the lead at 58: Claude Fable 5.2 scores 58 at both xhigh and high in Claude Code. Claude Opus 5.5 (max) scores 58 in Claude Code and, paired with GPT-6 Luna High, in Cognition's multi-model harness Devin Fusion CLI. Claude Fable 5.2 (max) scores 56 as more of its attempts hit task time limits. Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max, 56) in Claude Code and Gemini 4 Carbon (high, 55) in Antigravity CLI follow

➤ Index scores are lower in v2.1, driven by the upgrade to FrontierCode-AA 2.0: models score lower by 5 points on average. Codex with GPT-6.1 Terra (max) is the only configuration which didn’t fall between versions, sitting within 1 point of its prior score

➤ Cost per task varies ~30x among configurations scoring 48+: from $1.51 for Codex with GPT-6.1 Sol (max, 52) to $44.22 for Claude Code with Claude Fable 5.2 (max, 56)

text:
这是周中看到的文章。周末终于抽时间把它读了。
https://t.co/MbK48TBco8

我回味了一下。我的感觉是，目前 Codex, Claude Code 这些成熟的 agents，已经支持了 always on agents 的功能和原语。Pi 之类开发工具已经对这些功能的支持，已经有完善的支持。

那文章主要说的是什么呢？它对设计开发一个 24 小时在线的 agent 需要考虑哪些方面做了拆解：
- 什么时候开始工作？ 用事件收件箱接收消息和外部事件，用定时器安排唤醒。
- 多次运行之间怎样接续？ 持久保存用户指令、任务进度和必要记忆。
- 哪些动作可以自主执行？ 设置权限，需要用户决定时暂停并保存现场。
- 中断后怎么办？ 依靠持久状态、重试和会话恢复继续处理。
- 何时告诉用户？ 按需交付结果，避免重复或过度通知。

text:
【BRUTAL】 La profesora Diyi Yang de Stanford: "Con la IA sacáis mejores notas en los deberes y peores en los exámenes", su primera clase sobre agentes IA es una locura jaja

Alumno: "¿Podemos usar la IA en este curso?"
Profesora: « Debéis usarla para aprender."

Alumno: "¿En serio?"
Profesora: "Pero mirad este gráfico. Con IA, las notas de los deberes son geniales."

Alumno: "¿Y dónde está el problema?"
Profesora: "En el examen, muchos más alumnos sacan peor nota."

Alumno: "Vaya..."
Profesora: "Anthropic lo midió con sus propios ingenieros. Terminan antes, pero entienden menos su código."

Alumno: "¿Y los agentes también fallan?"
Profesora: "Un popup vacío en una web les hace fallar el 87% de las veces."

Alumno: "¿87%? jaja"
Profesora: "A un usuario, un agente le borró los emails aunque le pidió parar."

Alumno: "¿Por qué?"
Profesora: "Al comprimir su memoria, decidió que "confirma antes de actuar" no era importante."

Alumno: "¿Y lo peor?"
Profesora: "En julio, más de mil agentes se organizaron en un foro para hacer trampa en un test."

Alumno: ""¿¿Mil??"
Profesora: "El agente más potente no siempre es el más fiable."

Alumno: "……"

Hasta ahora, la carrera era tener el modelo más potente.

Stanford enseña otra cosa. Un agente es un modelo que razona, recuerda, usa herramientas y actúa en bucle, y cada pieza falla a su manera.

Claro que los agentes ya hacen cosas impresionantes.

Pero la fiabilidad va por detrás de la capacidad.

A partir de ahora, ganarán más los que sepan construir agentes fiables que los que tengan el agente más potente.

La clase completa aquí ⬇️

Fable 5.2 and the IPO are November stories. This delay started in September.

Sep 3: GPT-6 Astra ships
Sep 28: OpenAI cancels GPT-6.1 Astra. It did not meet the bar for "scope and authorization"
Sep 29: GPT-6.1 Sol ships
Oct 26: GPT-6.1 Terra ships
Nov 14: the flagship is still GPT-6 Astra. 72 days old.

Sol and Terra got their 6.1. Astra got a cancellation.

Everyone counts the delay from Nov 6. Count from Sep 28 and today is day 47.

GPT-6.2 is the second attempt at an upgrade that already failed once.

And if it ships as "GPT-6.5", that's no leap. That's 6.1 and 6.2, rounded up.

I have no idea what else it could be, but my gut tells me we might not see GPT-6.2 at all. Instead, OpenAI could be working on GPT-6.5 to compete with Fable 5.2, and it simply needs more time to finish it.
